newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia posts record 2.7 mln-bale cotton crop.
newsitem.headline: Australia posts record 2.7 mln-bale cotton crop.

text.p: Australia will process a record 2.7 million bales of cotton in 1996/97, the Cotton Australia industry group said on Friday.
"This is 500,000 bales more than the previous record of 2.2 million bales in 1992," it said.
The 1996/97 figure is equivalent to 612,000 tonnes of cotton and is valued at A$1.3 billion at the farm gate, Cotton Australia said.
The bumper harvest was the result of farmers taking on new technologies in farming, as the growing conditions in many areas were less than favourable, Cotton Australia said.
"There has always been concern that the bad start to the season, where many growing areas experienced unusually cold weather, would impact adversely on yields," the group said.
The successful harvest meant that cotton growers could plough more money into research and development to further improve yields, the group said.
"In 1997, this will be A$4.7 million from the research levy of A$1.75 a bale," Australia Cotton said.
Of the total harvest, New South Wales produced 1.9 million 500-lb bales, followed by Queensland producing the rest, Cotton Australia figures show.
About 92 percent of the crop will be exported, Cotton Australia said.
